proofs.proof_tex:
The mixed-support elimination theorem gives finite unions equal to the entire cycle fibers and an exact componentwise decision of whether \(\tau_C\) is constant. The established cycle-to-SCM lift gives
\[
\mathcal T_A(p,m)
=\{\tau_C(b,a):(b,a)\in\mathcal C_A(T)\},
\qquad
\mathcal T_B(p)
=\{\tau_C(b,a):(b,a,m,g,\pi)\in\mathcal C_B(T)\}. \tag{14}
\]
The compiler first tests its structural charts for nonemptiness. If no chart is nonempty, equality of the structural union with the cycle fiber implies that the corresponding fiber and target set are empty. Hence its cardinality is zero, not one; by the frozen definition this is an incompatible, nonrigid input, and the compiler reports incompatibility rather than an identifying or twin certificate.

Suppose next that the fiber is nonempty. By (14), \(|\mathcal T_A(p,m)|=1\) if and only if every design-A component projection is a singleton and all those singleton values agree. The identical argument with the residual-refined union proves the design-B equivalence. These are observable rank, support, incidence, residual, and cycle tests because every structural choice and every coefficient is constructed from \(T\), and from \(m\) when it is supplied.

For a real input, the evaluator works over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) relative to effective arithmetic and sign oracles. If field arithmetic actually constructs the common pair, the compiler returns that expression. Otherwise a singleton coordinate is encoded by a square-free real-univariate polynomial and Thom signs selecting its unique ordered value, even if that real value happens to lie in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\). For explicitly rational \(\zeta\), clearing denominators yields an integer polynomial, and exact real-root isolation supplies rational isolating intervals.

If the target image is not a singleton, the component algorithm returns two cycle points with unequal \(\tau_C\). Equation (14) and the established lift give two legal full SCMs with the same observables and supplied margins, when present, and unequal \(\tau\). When the nonrigid atlas stratum is interior, its strict sign chart supplies interior cycle samples, and the interior positive-lift lemma gives strictly positive twins. This proves every assertion.

Let \(R_{\mathrm{SYK}}(p)\) denote the pair in Appendix equations (A.28)--(A.33) of Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki. Consider a compatible observable law satisfying their Conditions 2--3. Every member of the present full fiber satisfies their Condition 1 by the defining response, selection, and proxy factorization. The cited regular-identification lemma therefore gives
\[
\tau(\vartheta)=R_{\mathrm{SYK}}(p)
\qquad\text{for every compatible }\vartheta. \tag{15}
\]
Compatibility makes the fiber nonempty, and the cited lemma includes the positive observed probabilities needed for every conditioning and division in (15). Hence the full target image is \(\{R_{\mathrm{SYK}}(p)\}\). The full-rigidity theorem makes \(\mathscr A\) declare the fiber rigid and return precisely this published value.

For any singular or boundary input, the completed structural enumeration first tests compatibility. If no chart is nonempty, its equality with the cycle fiber proves that the full fiber is empty by the cycle-to-SCM lift, and the compiler reports incompatibility. Otherwise, the rank-one normal forms, oriented rank-two faces, endpoint-incidence refinements, and support signs assign every design-A cycle point to a chart. In design B, the zero or active residual refinements additionally assign every compatible point to a residual forest and impose its component scales, cycle product, and relevance. The full-rigidity theorem then gives exactly one of two alternatives on the nonempty fiber: all one-copy component projections agree at an exact target value, or two sampled points lift to legal target-changing SCMs. This proves regular-domain agreement and the compatible boundary-coverage claim without applying the regular inversion outside its support.

Let \(\vartheta\in\mathcal F_B(p)\) satisfy the no-selection overlap and \(\mathcal K_{\mathrm K}(P_{\vartheta})\). The cited Kawakami identification lemma applies under the recursive factorization, invertibility, separation, and exclusion conditions included in \(\mathcal K_{\mathrm K}\); its simultaneous equations identify \(\omega_0^{\mathrm K}\) and \(\omega_1^{\mathrm K}\).

In the comparator order \((00,01,10,11)\), response consistency implies that \(X=1,Y=1\) admits precisely types \(01\) and \(11\), whereas \(X=0,Y=0\) admits precisely types \(00\) and \(01\). Selected-table positivity and \(S=1\) almost surely make both conditioning events positive. Therefore
\[
\operatorname{PN}(\vartheta)
=\frac{\omega^{\mathrm K}_{1,2}}
{\omega^{\mathrm K}_{1,2}+\omega^{\mathrm K}_{1,4}},
\qquad
\operatorname{PS}(\vartheta)
=\frac{\omega^{\mathrm K}_{0,2}}
{\omega^{\mathrm K}_{0,1}+\omega^{\mathrm K}_{0,2}}, \tag{16}
\]
which is \(\tau(\vartheta)=\phi_{\mathrm K}(\omega_0^{\mathrm K},\omega_1^{\mathrm K})\). If \(\mathcal T_B(p)\) is a singleton, it contains \(\tau(\vartheta)\) by definition; hence (16) is its unique value. The full-rigidity theorem makes the atlas value equal to that unique element. The cited Kawakami lemma also supplies the stated identified scope: the four joint binary potential-outcome-type probabilities and the treatment-conditional weights recovered in its proof.

For the boundary datum, the established experimental-proxy reduction and boundary-separation theorem gives
\[
\mathcal F_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})\ne\varnothing,
\qquad
\mathcal T_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})=\{(1/2,1/2)\}. \tag{17}
\]
For either \(x\), each row of \(A_x^{\mathrm K}(b^{\mathrm{bd}})\) is
\[
(1,b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}(w_1),b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}(w_2),b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}(w_3)).
\]
Because \(b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}\) is a probability vector on the three-point alphabet,
\[
1=b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}(w_1)+b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}(w_2)+b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}(w_3)
\]
row by row. Thus the first column of \(A_x^{\mathrm K}(b^{\mathrm{bd}})\) is the sum of its last three columns, so its determinant is zero for \(x=0,1\). The datum violates the named invertibility condition in Kawakami's Theorem 1(i), while (17) and the full atlas give a legal selected rigid law. This is a one-law strict scope separation and makes no subsumption claim.

Put \(H_0=k\ell+k+\ell+1\). A design-A chart can retain four normalized endpoint vectors and one coefficient row per edge, because the other is \(v_e-a_{ei}\). Design B additionally retains \(k-1\) projective coordinates, four margins, and at most four component scales. After harmless redundant coordinates are retained, the number of scalar variables is bounded by
\[
N=32H_0.
\]
The four table factorizations contribute \(4k\ell\) bilinear equations. Simplex, local-mode, support, incidence, residual-minor, forest, normalization, and relevance conditions bring the total number of input polynomials below \(128H_0\). If ratios are cleared only after their pivot signs have been declared, their degrees are at most eight, including the four-link cycle product.

For each edge there are two rank-two orientations or the rank-one labels \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm D\) and the \(3^k\) split faces of \(\mathrm E\). A deliberately loose bound for all four-edge choices, coordinate support signs, four residual pivots, and relevance signs is
\[
M_{k,\ell}
=(3^k+5)^4,3^{64H_0}(2k+1)^4(k^2+1). \tag{18}
\]
Thus the structural list is finite and explicitly enumerable. Its equality with the cycle fibers, proved in the mixed-support theorem, justifies discarding precisely the empty charts.

For a completely effective conservative bound, set
\[
D_0=8,\qquad S_0=128H_0,\qquad A_0=128H_0,
\]
and, for \(0\le j<N\), define
\[
D_{j+1}=2D_j^2,\qquad
S_{j+1}=4S_j^2D_j^2,\qquad
A_{j+1}=8S_jD_j^2(A_j+1). \tag{19}
\]
Finally define
\[
B_{k,\ell}
=M_{k,\ell}\bigl(1+D_N+S_N+A_N\bigr)^{N+2}. \tag{20}
\]
The cited real-algebraic algorithms terminate relative to arithmetic and sign oracles for the ordered coefficient field. The recurrences in (19) dominate, at each projection step, the degrees and counts created by derivatives, coefficients, discriminants, and pairwise resultants; \(A_j\) dominates the corresponding coefficient-height multiplier. Sign-invariant cells and their adjacency data compute the connected-component descriptions before any target projection. Real-univariate sampling and root isolation then use degrees no larger than the bound in (20). Thus (20) bounds the structural chart count, component count, and algebraic output degree and is a computable constant depending only on \((k,\ell)\).

For completeness, elementary induction in (19) gives
\[
\log_2D_j\le 4\,2^j,\qquad
\log_2S_j\le 2^{2j+8}(H_0+1),\qquad
\log_2A_j\le 2^{2j+10}(H_0+1).
\]
Since \(N=32H_0\), equations (18)--(20) imply, for example,
\[
B_{k,\ell}\le 2^{2^{128H_0}}. \tag{21}
\]
Thus the theorem's universal constant may be taken as \(C=128\).

Now suppose the input is rational with numerator and denominator bit length at most \(L\). Clearing input denominators and forming normalized columns, minors, and chart polynomials gives initial integer coefficient height at most \(A_0(L+1)=128H_0(L+1)\). The same determinant and resultant estimates underlying (19) bound every projected coefficient height by \(A_N(L+1)\). Standard signed-subresultant root isolation from the cited source produces rational isolating endpoints with bit length bounded by this height times a polynomial in \(D_N\); (20) absorbs that polynomial. Square-free factorization cannot increase degree. Enlarging the already fixed numerical constant \(128\), if necessary, gives
\[
\text{degree}\le B_{k,\ell},
\qquad
\text{bit length}\le B_{k,\ell}(L+1)^{128}. \tag{22}
\]
All calls after structural enumeration concern a single chart or its one-copy target graph. No two-copy unequal-target formula occurs, proving the method and bounds claimed.

Let \(K\) be a compact subset of \(\mathfrak R_{\varepsilon}\). Compactness and selected-table positivity bound all true multinomial cell probabilities away from zero. The cited multinomial central limit theorem and the independent-sample scaling give, at each law,
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta)\Rightarrow N(0,\Omega_{\zeta}),
\qquad
\widehat\Omega_n\xrightarrow{P}\Omega_{\zeta}. \tag{23}
\]
These conclusions are uniform on \(K\). Indeed, if uniformity failed, one could choose a sequence of laws in \(K\) witnessing failure and then a convergent subsequence. For categorical summands, boundedness makes the Lindeberg remainder uniform, and their covariance matrices converge along that subsequence; the same subsequence argument applies to the polynomial plug-in covariance. This contradicts the pointwise theorem at the subsequential limit.

For every incident chart \(\chi\), \(d_\chi(\zeta)=0\). Since distance to a closed set is one-Lipschitz,
\[
d_\chi(\widehat\zeta_n)
\le\|\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta\|_2
=O_P(n^{-1/2})=o_P(t_n),
\qquad t_n=n^{-1/4}. \tag{24}
\]
Continuity of the finitely many normalized slacks and \(\eta_\chi(\zeta)\ge\varepsilon\) makes the slack test exceed \(\varepsilon/2\) with probability tending to one. Conversely, the \(\varepsilon\)-distance from incompatible chart closures gives
\[
d_\chi(\widehat\zeta_n)
\ge\varepsilon-\|\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta\|_2>t_n
\]
with probability tending to one for every incompatible chart. By the definition of \(\mathfrak R_{\varepsilon}\), every qualifying chart outside the incident first-order-compatible family is an incompatible chart and is therefore covered by this separation. Finiteness of the atlas and compactness of \(K\) make the preceding probability bounds uniform. Thus the lexicographic selector chooses an incident first-order-compatible rigid chart with probability tending to one, uniformly on \(K\). All eligible incident charts have the common target and Jacobian required by \(\mathfrak R_{\varepsilon}\).

On the selected chart, Taylor's theorem for the twice continuously differentiable extension gives
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau)
=J_\chi(\zeta)\sqrt n(\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta)+o_P(1), \tag{25}
\]
uniformly on \(K\); bounded second derivatives on finitely many compact neighborhoods make the remainder uniform. The common-value and common-Jacobian condition makes (25) independent of the lexicographic choice. Equations (23)--(25) and the cited delta method yield
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau)\Rightarrow N(0,V_\tau),
\qquad
V_\tau=J_\chi(\zeta)\Omega_\zeta J_\chi(\zeta)^{\top}. \tag{26}
\]
Continuity of the finitely many Jacobians and (23) also gives
\[
\widehat V_n
=J_{\widehat\chi_n}(\widehat\zeta_n)
\widehat\Omega_n
J_{\widehat\chi_n}(\widehat\zeta_n)^{\top}
\xrightarrow{P}V_\tau. \tag{27}
\]
The lower bound \(\lambda_{\min}(V_\tau)\ge\varepsilon\) and (27) imply positive definiteness of the raw sandwich matrix with probability tending to one, so \(\widehat\gamma_n=1\) with that probability. The quadratic form in (26)--(27) converges to \(\chi^2_2\); every fixed nonzero scalar contrast has positive limiting variance and its standardized form converges to \(N(0,1)\). The elliptical branch of \(W_n\), and the corresponding usual scalar Wald intervals, therefore have limiting coverage \(1-\alpha\).

If no chart is certified, the definitions give \(\widehat\chi_n=\bot\), \(F_\bot=(0,0)\), \(J_\bot=0\), \(\widehat\tau_n=(0,0)\), \(\widehat V_n=I_2\), and \(W_n=[0,1]^2\). No covariance-consistency or Wald assertion is made for that fallback branch. This proves the theorem.

Let \(q_0\) denote the true observable law, including the independent margin law in design A when it is sampled, and put \(t_0=\tau(\vartheta)\). By the definition of the corresponding full fiber and target set,
\[
t_0\in\mathcal T(q_0). \tag{28}
\]
Each multinomial cell count is marginally binomial. A two-sided Clopper--Pearson interval inverts its two exact binomial tail tests, so its two noncoverage tails are bounded by their allocated probabilities. Bonferroni's inequality over all selected-table and independent-margin cells therefore gives
\[
P_{q_0}\{q_0\notin C_n\}\le\beta_n. \tag{29}
\]
No rank, compatibility-neighborhood, or identification condition is used here.

For a fixed compatible pair \((q,t)\), define
\[
G_{q,t}=P_q\{\Delta_n^{\mathrm{rep}}(t)
\ge\Delta_n^{\mathrm{obs}}(t)\mid\Delta_n^{\mathrm{obs}}(t)\}.
\]
The discrete upper-tail lemma applied to the replicate statistic gives
\[
P_q(G_{q,t}\le u)\le u\qquad(0\le u\le1). \tag{30}
\]
On \(\{q_0\in C_n\}\), equations (28) and the supremum in \(\operatorname{pv}_n\) imply
\[
\operatorname{pv}_n(t_0)
\ge\min\{1,\beta_n+G_{q_0,t_0}\}. \tag{31}
\]
Since \(\beta_n\le\alpha/2\), exclusion of \(t_0\) from \(K_n\), together with (29)--(31), yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_{q_0}\{t_0\notin K_n\}
&\le P_{q_0}\{q_0\notin C_n\}
 +P_{q_0}\{G_{q_0,t_0}\le\alpha-\beta_n\}\\
&\le\beta_n+(\alpha-\beta_n)=\alpha.
\end{aligned} \tag{32}
\]
This is a finite-sample statement containing no continuity constant. Applying it at each index of an arbitrary triangular array proves the same bound along sequences approaching \(\mathfrak D\).

We now prove the narrowed first-order assertion rather than importing it from a generic likelihood theorem. Fix a compact locally saturated subset \(K\subset\mathfrak R_{\varepsilon}\). Write \(I_\zeta=\Omega_\zeta^{-1}\) in reduced coordinates; compact interior positivity makes its eigenvalues uniformly bounded above and below. For \(q=\zeta+h/\sqrt n\), with bounded \(h\), a third-order Taylor expansion of each term \(N_j\log q_j\), with the simplex reference coordinate restored, gives uniformly on \(K\)
\[
2\{\ell_n(\widehat\zeta_n)-\ell_n(q)\}
=n(q-\widehat\zeta_n)^{\top}I_\zeta(q-\widehat\zeta_n)+o_P(1). \tag{33}
\]
The remainder is uniform because all probabilities are bounded away from zero and the finite-alphabet third derivatives are uniformly bounded. The two-sample version is the sum of two such expansions and has the block information corresponding to \(\Omega_\zeta\).

Local saturation says that, in a common ambient neighborhood, the restriction \(t\in\mathcal T(q)\) is the finite union of equations \(t=F_\chi(q)\) over incident charts, with no further equality restriction on \(q\). Their common first derivative is \(J_\chi(\zeta)\), and the \(C^2\) condition gives
\[
F_\chi(q)=\tau+J_\chi(\zeta)(q-\zeta)+O(\|q-\zeta\|_2^2) \tag{34}
\]
uniformly over the finite incident family. Positive definiteness of \(V_\tau=J_\chi\Omega_\zeta J_\chi^{\top}\) makes \(J_\chi\) have row rank two. Local saturation then also places the target in the relative interior of \([0,1]^2\): otherwise a full-row-rank linear image of an ambient neighborhood would cross a boundary of the square. On a compact set the distance from that boundary is uniform. Minimizing the quadratic in (33) subject to the linearization in (34) gives, by the Lagrange-multiplier equations,
\[
\Delta_n(t)
=n(t-\widehat\tau_n)^{\top}
\widehat V_n^{-1}(t-\widehat\tau_n)+o_P(1) \tag{35}
\]
uniformly for \(\|t-\tau\|_2=O(n^{-1/2})\). The common value and Jacobian make the leading term identical on every incident graph; the positive eigenvalue bound makes it uniformly coercive. The same coercivity and (33) show that accepted targets lie in an \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\) neighborhood.

For a replicate generated under any \(q\) in that shrinking neighborhood with \(t\in\mathcal T(q)\), the centered empirical vector has the uniform multinomial normal limit established by the subsequence argument in the separated-Wald proof. Applying the same quadratic minimization to the replicate version of (35) gives a \(\chi^2_2\) limit uniformly in \((q,t)\). Moreover, the Clopper--Pearson region has \(\sup_{q\in C_n}\|q-q_0\|_2=O_P(\sqrt{\log n/n})=o_P(1)\): this follows directly from the binomial likelihood-ratio or Chernoff bound at tail allocation of order \(n^{-2}\), uniformly on the interior compact set. Hence the supremum replicate tail in \(\operatorname{pv}_n(t)\) converges uniformly on the root-\(n\) boundary to the \(\chi^2_2\) upper tail, and \(\beta_n\to0\). Consequently
\[
K_n=
\left\{t\in[0,1]^2:
n(t-\widehat\tau_n)^{\top}\widehat V_n^{-1}
(t-\widehat\tau_n)
\le\chi^2_{2,1-\alpha}+o_P(1)
\right\} \tag{36}
\]
in root-\(n\) Hausdorff scale. Since the eigenvalues of \(\widehat V_n\) are bounded away from zero and infinity with probability tending to one, an \(o_P(1)\) perturbation of the quadratic level moves its boundary by \(o_P(n^{-1/2})\). Comparing (36) with \(W_n\) proves
\[
\sqrt n\,d_{\mathrm H}(K_n,W_n)\xrightarrow{P}0.
\]

The local-saturation qualification is necessary for this particular deviance and Wald pair. If the observable chart has codimension \(r>0\), the quadratic minimization of (33) includes an additional nonnegative model-fit term in the normal directions. The replicate deviance then has \(r+2\), rather than two, first-order quadratic degrees of freedom, and the realized model-fit term changes the root-\(n\) profile radius. The conditions defining \(\mathfrak R_{\varepsilon}\) control target covariance and chart separation but do not exclude such lower-dimensional rank charts. Thus outside the locally saturated subclass, (32) remains valid but no Hausdorff equivalence to the frozen \(W_n\) is asserted.

theorem.statement: For every fixed finite \((\mathcal W,\mathcal Z)\), the compiler \(\mathscr A\) can be completed as follows. Its design-A charts have coordinates \((b,a)\) and form an exhaustive finite disjoint structural atlas for every nonempty \(\mathcal C_A(T)\) by combining the two oriented rank-two segment modes with the four rank-one modes \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm E,\mathrm D\), all split-coordinate faces of \(\mathrm E\), all coefficient and endpoint support faces, and all endpoint-incidence pivot signs, while using one shared variable \(b_i\) at the two cells incident to response type \(i\). For \(\mathcal C_B(T)\) it adjoins \(\rho>0\), the zero-residual or lexicographically pivoted active negative-proportional state at every response type, residual-forest propagation, the active four-cycle product, positive component scales with normalization, and the relevance inequality. These unions equal \(\mathcal C_A(T)\) and \(\mathcal C_B(T)\), respectively, including simultaneous rank-one cells, coincident endpoints, inactive rows, and forced-zero faces. On each resulting one-copy chart, connected-component descriptions are computed first; the componentwise graph of \(\tau_C\) is then projected and tested for constancy, and the constants are compared across all components and faces. Relative to effective arithmetic and sign oracles for \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), the procedure returns either a common exact value or two legal target-changing full-SCM lifts. A field expression is returned only when it is actually constructed by field arithmetic; otherwise the value is returned by a real-univariate representation and Thom signs, even if the represented value happens to belong to \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\). Target-changing lifts may lie on boundary faces and are strictly positive when sampled from an interior support chart. No two-copy unequal-target quantifier-elimination predicate is used in constructing or classifying the structural atlas.
theorem.proof_tex:
Write \(k=|\mathcal Z|\), \(\ell=|\mathcal W|\), and fix orders of cells, response types, proxy coordinates, and instrument coordinates. Selected-table positivity implies
\[
r_e>0,\qquad v_e(z)>0,
\qquad c_{ez}:=\frac{T_e(\cdot,z)}{v_e(z)}\in\Delta_{\mathcal W}^{\circ}. \tag{2}
\]
Every matrix in a two-column nonnegative factorization has rank at most two. Since (2) rules out rank zero, nonemptiness of either cycle fiber implies \(\operatorname{rank}(T_e)\in\{1,2\}\) for every cell. The ranks and all equalities among the observed normalized columns are determined by minors over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).

\emph{Rank-two local charts.} Suppose \(\mathcal I_e=\{i,j\}\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(T_e)=2\). In any factorization, division by \(v_e(z)>0\) gives
\[
c_{ez}=q_{ez}b_i+(1-q_{ez})b_j,
\qquad q_{ez}:=a_{ei}(z)/v_e(z)\in[0,1]. \tag{3}
\]
Rank two forces \(b_i\ne b_j\), and (3) says that all observed column points lie in the closed segment with those endpoints. Conversely, if two distinct probability vectors on the observed affine line bracket every \(c_{ez}\), equation (3) has unique coefficients in \([0,1]\), and multiplication by \(v_e(z)\) gives the unique nonnegative cell coefficients.

Choose the lexicographically first proxy coordinate \(h_e\) which is nonconstant on the observed column points. It exists because the normalized columns span an affine line. In the orientation \(b_i(h_e)<b_j(h_e)\), the exact chart conditions and coefficient formula are
\[
b_i(h_e)\le\min_z c_{ez}(h_e),\qquad
b_j(h_e)\ge\max_z c_{ez}(h_e),
\qquad
q_{ez}=\frac{b_j(h_e)-c_{ez}(h_e)}{b_j(h_e)-b_i(h_e)}. \tag{4}
\]
The reverse orientation interchanges the inequalities. The denominator in (4) has a declared strict sign, so clearing it preserves every inequality and produces polynomial chart conditions over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\). The two orientations are disjoint and exhaustive. Splitting each \(q_{ez}\) into \(0\), \((0,1)\), or \(1\) records every endpoint equality and forced coefficient zero. This is the local segment construction underlying the established rank-two orientation theorem, retained edge by edge.

\emph{Rank-one local charts.} If \(\operatorname{rank}(T_e)=1\), the rank-one normal-form lemma applies by (2). Hence the cell is in exactly one of \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm E,\mathrm D\). In particular, an inactive row leaves its unused endpoint as an arbitrary point of \(\Delta_{\mathcal W}\); it is not silently placed in the span of the observed tables. In mode \(\mathrm E\), every vector \(s_e\) is retained, and its \(3^k\) coordinate faces exhaust \(0\le s_e\le v_e\). In mode \(\mathrm D\), \(q_e\in(0,1)\) remains a chart variable. Thus no instrument information carried by an equal-endpoint split is discarded.

\emph{Global design-A union.} Take the product of the local mode choices over the four response-cycle edges, using one global variable \(b_i\), rather than separate copies, at the two cells incident to response type \(i\). Add
\[
b_i(w)\ge0,\qquad \sum_w b_i(w)=1, \tag{5}
\]
and refine by the signs of the following finite family: every \(b_i(w)\); every \(a_{ei}(z)\) and \(v_e(z)-a_{ei}(z)\); every coordinate of \(b_i-b_j\) and \(b_i-c_e\) appearing in a rank-one mode; the pivot minors comparing an endpoint displacement with each incident observed-line direction; and every pivot or denominator used in (4). A nonzero vector uses its lexicographically first nonzero coordinate as pivot. Zero is separated from each strict sign. Coincident lines and endpoints, endpoint incidences, inactive vertices, and all support faces are therefore included in finitely many disjoint sign refinements. Where two closed rank-two orientation boxes share a face, assign that face to the lexicographically first compatible label; this changes neither their union nor their defining semialgebraicity.

Let the resulting sets be \(X^A_\gamma(T)\). If \((b,a)\in\mathcal C_A(T)\), its ranks choose a mode at every edge; (3)--(4) choose one rank-two orientation and coefficient face; the rank-one lemma chooses one rank-one mode and split face; and the actual signs choose one global refinement. Because the same actual \(b_i\) is used at both incident cells, the point lies in one \(X^A_\gamma(T)\). Thus
\[
\mathcal C_A(T)\subseteq\bigcup_\gamma X^A_\gamma(T). \tag{6}
\]
Conversely, (3)--(5) and the rank-one formulas give normalized nonnegative endpoints and coefficients, \(a_{ei}+a_{ej}=v_e\), and \(T_e=b_ia_{ei}^{\top}+b_ja_{ej}^{\top}\) on every edge. Hence every chart point is in \(\mathcal C_A(T)\), proving equality in (6). This is equality of the full nonnegative fiber, not merely a dense or generic subset.

\emph{Global design-B union.} Fix a baseline \(z_0\) and adjoin \(\rho_{z_0}=1\), \(\rho_z>0\). At response type \(i\), order its incident cells as \((e_i,f_i)\). There are exactly two feasible residual states. The zero state is
\[
D^{\mathrm{res}}_{e_i i}(\rho)=D^{\mathrm{res}}_{f_i i}(\rho)=0. \tag{7}
\]
For an active state, choose the lexicographically first coordinate \(h\ne z_0\) at which \(D^{\mathrm{res}}_{e_i i,h}\ne0\), choose its sign, and impose
\[
\begin{gathered}
D^{\mathrm{res}}_{e_i i,h}D^{\mathrm{res}}_{f_i i,h}<0,\\
D^{\mathrm{res}}_{e_i i,u}D^{\mathrm{res}}_{f_i i,h}
-D^{\mathrm{res}}_{e_i i,h}D^{\mathrm{res}}_{f_i i,u}=0
\quad(u\ne z_0),\\
R_i:=-\frac{D^{\mathrm{res}}_{e_i i,h}}
{D^{\mathrm{res}}_{f_i i,h}}>0,
\qquad m_{f_i}=R_im_{e_i}.
\end{gathered} \tag{8}
\]
All preceding residual coordinates are zero. Thus the pivot choices are finite and disjoint and express exactly that the residuals are nonzero and negatively proportional. A state with exactly one zero residual is excluded.

The active links form a subgraph of the four-cycle on the cell vertices. Every proper subgraph is a forest. In each forest component choose its least cell as root, multiply the ratios \(R_i\) along the unique root-to-cell path, and write
\[
m_e=\lambda_C R_e,\qquad \lambda_C>0,\qquad
\sum_C\lambda_C\sum_{e\in C}R_e=1, \tag{9}
\]
where \(R_e=1\) at a root. If all four links are active, use a spanning tree in (9) and impose that the product of the four directed ratios around the cycle equals one. Every denominator has a declared nonzero sign, so (8)--(9) are equivalent to finite polynomial sign conditions. Finally set
\[
g(z)=\frac{\rho_z}{\sum_u\rho_u},\qquad
q^X_z=\sum_{e:e_X=1}m_e\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_e}a_{ei}(z), \tag{10}
\]
and refine the relevance disjunction by the lexicographically first pair and sign for which
\[
q^X_z\rho_{z'}-q^X_{z'}\rho_z\ne0. \tag{11}
\]
The established IV residual-forest theorem proves both directions: every point of \(\mathcal C_B(T)\) has exactly one state (7) or (8) at every response type, its positive margins have representation (9), every active cycle obeys the product constraint, and relevance gives (11); conversely (7)--(11) reconstruct positive margins satisfying all shared-\(Z\) equations, a normalized positive \(g\), response weights \(\pi\), and relevance. Combining this with (6) gives
\[
\mathcal C_B(T)=\bigcup_\delta X^B_\delta(T). \tag{12}
\]
Equations (7) and (9) retain zero-residual vertices and free component scales, so (12) covers simultaneous inactive-row and hidden-split patterns.

\emph{One-copy component evaluation and gluing.} For either design and every nonempty chart \(X_\gamma\), first apply the cited effective component algorithm to \(X_\gamma\) itself. It returns descriptions and samples for all of its semialgebraically connected components. Only after those components have been computed, for each component \(C\) form the one-copy graph
\[
G_{\gamma,C}=
\left\{(x,t):x\in C,\quad
t_1=\sum_z a_{11,2}(z),\quad
t_2=\sum_z a_{00,2}(z)\right\}. \tag{13}
\]
All variables in (13) occur once. Its coefficients belong to \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), and its target equations are linear. Project each restricted graph onto each target coordinate. A sign-invariant decomposition decides whether both projections are singletons. If a projection is not a singleton, it contains two distinct sample cells; sample one target value in each and then sample the corresponding one-copy inverse fibers. This returns two points of \(C\) with different target values without introducing a two-copy predicate. If both coordinate projections are singletons, the target is constant on \(C\). Compare their real-univariate encodings by Thom signs across every component and chart.

By (6) and (12), constancy on every component and equality of all component constants are necessary and sufficient for constancy of \(\tau_C\) on the entire cycle fiber. A singleton semialgebraic set defined over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) consists of elements algebraic over that field. Relative to effective field arithmetic and sign oracles, the exact algorithms return a field expression only if their arithmetic construction produces one. Otherwise they return a square-free real-univariate representation and Thom signs, without attempting to decide whether the represented real number happens to lie in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).

If constancy fails, the two sampled cycle points either come from one nonconstant component projection or from components with unequal constants. The established cycle-to-SCM lift maps them to legal full SCMs with identical observables and, in design A, identical supplied margins, while preserving \(\tau=\tau_C\). On an interior support chart the sampling cells can be chosen within the strict sign region; the interior positive-lift lemma then gives strictly positive twins. Boundary or cross-face comparisons require only legal nonnegative twins.

The construction before (13) uses only the enumerated response-cycle modes, shared endpoints, residual states, forest ratios, and relevance. Real-algebraic machinery is applied separately to the one-copy graph of each already exhaustive component. No formula with two factorization copies and an unequal-target predicate is used. This proves the stated completion of \(\mathscr A\).

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(e\in\mathcal E\) have \(\mathcal I_e=\{i,j\}\), and suppose that \(T_e\) has rank one. Put \(c_e=T_e(\cdot,z)/v_e(z)\), which is independent of \(z\). Every factorization of this cell in \(\mathcal C_A(T)\) belongs to exactly one of the following disjoint modes, with the coincident case assigned to mode \(\mathrm E\):
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(\mathrm L)&a_{ei}\equiv0,\quad b_j=c_e,\quad b_i\ne c_e;\\
(\mathrm R)&a_{ej}\equiv0,\quad b_i=c_e,\quad b_j\ne c_e;\\
(\mathrm E)&b_i=b_j=c_e,\quad a_{ei}(z)=s_e(z),\quad
             a_{ej}(z)=v_e(z)-s_e(z),\quad0\le s_e(z)\le v_e(z);\\
(\mathrm D)&b_i\ne b_j,\quad c_e=q_e b_i+(1-q_e)b_j,\quad
             a_{ei}(z)=q_ev_e(z),\quad a_{ej}(z)=(1-q_e)v_e(z),
             \quad0<q_e<1.
\end{array}
\]
Conversely, every parameter tuple in one of these modes is a valid rank-one cell factorization. Mode \(\mathrm E\) is the disjoint union of the \(3^{|\mathcal Z|}\) split-coordinate faces obtained by declaring, for each \(z\), exactly one of \(s_e(z)=0\), \(0<s_e(z)<v_e(z)\), and \(s_e(z)=v_e(z)\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Selected-table positivity gives \(T_e(w,z)>0\) and therefore
\[
v_e(z)=\sum_{w\in\mathcal W}T_e(w,z)>0
\qquad(z\in\mathcal Z).
\]
Because \(T_e\) is nonzero and has rank one, all of its columns are positive multiples of one positive probability vector. Normalization by their positive sums consequently gives a single vector \(c_e\in\Delta_{\mathcal W}^{\circ}\) such that
\[
T_e(\cdot,z)=v_e(z)c_e
\qquad(z\in\mathcal Z).
\]
For a cell factorization define
\[
q_z=\frac{a_{ei}(z)}{v_e(z)}\in[0,1].
\]
The division is legitimate because \(v_e(z)>0\), and the interval assertion follows from nonnegativity and \(a_{ei}(z)+a_{ej}(z)=v_e(z)\). Dividing the factorization equation by \(v_e(z)\) yields
\[
c_e=q_zb_i+(1-q_z)b_j. \tag{1}
\]
If \(b_i=b_j\), equation (1) and normalization give \(b_i=b_j=c_e\), while the only remaining restriction is \(0\le a_{ei}(z)\le v_e(z)\). This is exactly mode \(\mathrm E\), with \(s_e(z)=a_{ei}(z)\).

Suppose instead that \(b_i\ne b_j\). Subtracting (1) at two coordinates \(z,z'\) gives
\[
(q_z-q_{z'})(b_i-b_j)=0.
\]
Since \(b_i-b_j\ne0\), it follows that \(q_z=q_{z'}\) for every pair; write the common value as \(q_e\). If \(q_e=0\), then \(a_{ei}\equiv0\), \(a_{ej}=v_e\), and (1) gives \(b_j=c_e\). The assumed endpoint inequality gives \(b_i\ne c_e\), so this is mode \(\mathrm L\). The case \(q_e=1\) is symmetrically mode \(\mathrm R\). If \(0<q_e<1\), equation (1) and the displayed coefficient identities give mode \(\mathrm D\). The alternatives are mutually exclusive by the endpoint equality and the three disjoint possibilities for \(q_e\). Direct substitution proves the converse in every case. Finally, since \(v_e(z)>0\), the three stated alternatives for each coordinate of \(s_e\) are disjoint and exhaustive; their Cartesian product has \(3^{|\mathcal Z|}\) members.

added_lemmas.statement: Let \(K\) be an ordered subfield of \(\mathbb R\). Given effective arithmetic and sign oracles for \(K\), let a semialgebraic set in \(N\) variables be described by a Boolean combination of sign conditions on \(s\) polynomials of degree at most \(d\) over \(K\). Sign determination, quantifier elimination, real-univariate sampling, cylindrical decomposition, and roadmap algorithms decide emptiness, compute projections and semialgebraically connected-component descriptions, and return sample points meeting all components. Exact outputs can be represented by square-free univariate polynomials over \(K\), rational functions of a selected root, and Thom signs. For fixed \((N,s,d)\) these procedures terminate, and their arithmetic, degree, and integer-input bit complexity admit effective bounds obtained from the projection, sampling, and roadmap recurrences.

added_lemmas.statement: Let the selected table be positive. In design A, suppose \((b,a)\in\mathcal C_A(T)\), the supplied margin vector is positive, and \(b_i(w)>0\) and \(a_{ei}(z)>0\) for every proxy coordinate and every incident triple. Then the cycle-to-SCM lift can be chosen so that every response mass and every nonstructural kernel coordinate is strictly positive: \(\pi_i>0\), \(b_i(w)>0\), \(g_i(z)>0\), \(0<e_i(z)<1\), and \(0<s_e<1\). The analogous assertion holds for an interior point of \(\mathcal C_B(T)\), with its positive \(m\) and common positive \(g\). Thus two interior cycle points with different \(\tau_C\)-values lift to strictly positive legal full SCM twins with the same supplied information.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Consider design A. By compatible-margin positivity, every supplied margin of a nonempty fiber is positive. For an interior cycle point define, as in the established lift,
\[
h_i(z)=\sum_{e:i\in\mathcal I_e}m_ea_{ei}(z),
\qquad
\pi_i=\sum_z h_i(z).
\]
Each response type is incident to two cells. Since every summand is positive, \(h_i(z)>0\) and \(\pi_i>0\). Hence \(g_i(z)=h_i(z)/\pi_i>0\). Exactly one incident cell for type \(i\) has treatment coordinate one and exactly one has treatment coordinate zero. Therefore the lift's assignment probability is
\[
e_i(z)=\frac{m_{e_1(i)}a_{e_1(i),i}(z)}{h_i(z)},
\]
where both the numerator and the omitted other-cell contribution to the denominator are positive. Consequently \(0<e_i(z)<1\). The endpoint kernels \(b_i(w)\) are positive by hypothesis.

Put
\[
c_0=\frac12\min_{e\in\mathcal E}\frac{m_e}{r_e}>0,
\qquad
s_e=\frac{c_0r_e}{m_e}.
\]
All divisions are legitimate because selected-table positivity gives \(r_e>0\) and margin positivity gives \(m_e>0\). Moreover \(0<s_e\le1/2<1\). The construction in the cycle-to-SCM lift now gives a legal member of \(\mathcal F_A(p,m)\) with precisely the asserted strict inequalities.

For design B, membership in \(\mathcal C_B(T)\) already supplies positive \(m\) and a common positive \(g\). The same formulas give \(h_i(z)>0\), \(\pi_i>0\), and \(0<e_i(z)<1\), while the displayed choice of \(c_0\) again gives \(0<s_e<1\). The established lift preserves \(\tau=\tau_C\) and all supplied observables. Applying it separately to two interior cycle points therefore gives the claimed strictly positive twins.

added_lemmas.statement:
Under independent multinomial sampling, at every fixed interior observable coordinate \(\zeta\), the reduced empirical-frequency vector satisfies
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta)\Rightarrow N(0,\Omega_{\zeta}),
\qquad
\widehat\Omega_n\xrightarrow{P}\Omega_{\zeta},
\]
where, for two independent multinomial samples with \(n/n_m\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)\), the joint covariance is block diagonal and the margin block is multiplied by \(\lambda\). Continuously differentiable maps obey the multivariate delta method, and an interior multinomial log likelihood is locally asymptotically quadratic.

attestation.note: Used only for the finite-dimensional central limit, delta-method, and LAN substrate; compact-uniform chart and Hausdorff conclusions are derived in this solve.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(R\) be any real-valued statistic with an arbitrary, possibly discrete, distribution, let \(R'\) be an independent copy, and define \(G(R)=P(R'\ge R)\). Then
\[
P\{G(R)\le u\}\le u
\qquad(0\le u\le1).
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The case \(u=1\) is immediate. For \(0\le u<1\), let \(H(x)=P(R\ge x)\), a nonincreasing tail function. If \(A_u=\{x:H(x)\le u\}\) is empty, the result is immediate. Otherwise \(H(x)\to1\) as \(x\to-\infty\), so \(x_u=\inf A_u\) is finite. The event \(H(R)\le u\) is contained in \(\{R\ge x_u\}\); if the infimum is not attained, it is contained in \(\{R>x_u\}\). In the attained case,
\[
P\{H(R)\le u\}\le P(R\ge x_u)=H(x_u)\le u.
\]
In the nonattained case choose \(x_j\downarrow x_u\) with \(x_j\in A_u\). Then continuity from below gives
\[
P(R>x_u)=\lim_{j\to\infty}P(R\ge x_j)\le u.
\]
Since conditioning on \(R\) gives \(P(R'\ge R\mid R)=H(R)=G(R)\), the displayed inequality is the claim.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: The compiler first reports incompatibility if the relevant full fiber is empty; then the target set has cardinality zero and the input is not rigid. On a nonempty design-A fiber, \(|\mathcal T_A(p,m)|=1\) if and only if the finite observable rank/support/cycle conditions returned by \(\mathscr A(T,m)\) hold. On a nonempty design-B fiber, \(|\mathcal T_B(p)|=1\) if and only if the corresponding residual-forest and cycle conditions returned by \(\mathscr A(T)\) hold. For an arbitrary real input \(\zeta\), if field arithmetic actually constructs a rigid value, the compiler may return that expression in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\); otherwise it returns a uniquely ordered real element of a finite algebraic extension, certified by a square-free polynomial in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}[q]\) and Thom sign data, even when the represented value happens to lie in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\). If \(\zeta\) is explicitly rational, this certificate may instead be normalized to a square-free integer polynomial and rational isolating interval. Every compatible nonrigid output contains two legal full SCMs with identical observables and supplied margins, when supplied, but different \(\tau\); both SCMs are strictly positive whenever the nonrigid stratum is interior.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Under the frozen definition an empty target set has cardinality zero and is therefore not rigid, but it cannot contain a target-changing pair. The repaired claim separates incompatibility from compatible nonrigidity and makes the exact-output branch return a field expression only when that expression is actually constructed.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: On every observable law satisfying Conditions 2--3 of Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki (2026) that is compatible with the selected four-response-type model, the rigid value returned by \(\mathscr A\) equals the PN/PS value obtained from their Appendix equations (A.28)--(A.33). The same atlas is defined on singular and boundary inputs not covered by those regular conditions, including design-A support-face strata with rank loss, coincident endpoints, inactive rows, or forced-zero incident coefficients and analogous design-B strata governed by response-level shared-\(Z\) residual forests. It reports incompatibility when the full fiber is empty; on every nonempty such fiber it returns either a target-rigidity certificate with an exact value or a legal target-changing full-SCM certificate.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The published Conditions 2--3 do not by themselves assert that an arbitrary observable table has a compatible Condition-1 SCM. The repaired claim conditions regular-formula agreement on compatibility and adds the required separate incompatibility output for empty fibers.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For fixed \(k=|\mathcal Z|\) and \(\ell=|\mathcal W|\), the finite structural chart enumeration of \(\mathscr A\) terminates. For an arbitrary real input this computation is relative to effective arithmetic and sign oracles for \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\). There is an explicit recursively computable constant \(B_{k,\ell}\le 2^{2^{C(k\ell+k+\ell+1)}}\), for a universal numerical constant \(C\), bounding the number of labeled charts and the algebraic degree over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\). If every coordinate of \(\zeta\) is an explicitly encoded rational whose numerator and denominator have binary length at most \(L\), a Turing implementation terminates; after clearing denominators, every algebraic target certificate uses a square-free integer polynomial of degree at most \(B_{k,\ell}\) and rational isolating endpoints, and every coefficient and endpoint has bit length at most \(B_{k,\ell}(L+1)^C\). The classification is obtained from the structural charts in \(\mathscr A\), not from generic two-copy quantifier elimination.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: For an arbitrary coefficient field generated by real inputs, an algorithmic claim is meaningful only relative to effective field arithmetic and sign oracles. The revised text makes that qualification explicit and replaces an unsupported nominal bound by the recursively computed conservative bound proved here.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For the Clopper--Pearson preliminary region \(C_n\), profile discrepancy \(\Delta_n\), and Berger--Boos calibration in \(\operatorname{pv}_n\), \(P_{\vartheta}\{\tau(\vartheta)\in K_n\}\ge1-\alpha\) at every sample size for every \(\vartheta\) in either design. The bound holds along arbitrary sequences approaching \(\mathfrak D\), including point-to-set transitions. Uniformly over compact subsets of \(\mathfrak R_{\varepsilon}\) that are locally saturated in the following explicit sense---there is a common neighborhood of each \(\zeta\) on which, for observable coordinate \(q\), the compatible target correspondence is the finite union of the incident graphs \(t=F_\chi(q)\), with no additional observable equality restriction---one has \(\sqrt n\,d_{\mathrm H}(K_n,W_n)\xrightarrow{P}0\). On those locally saturated strata the profile boundary and the Wald ellipse have the same first-order quadratic expansion and \(\chi^2_{2,1-\alpha}\) calibration. At a law with a non-singleton identified set, without the separated-chart conditions, or on a lower-dimensional observable chart, the theorem asserts coverage only and makes no claim that \(\operatorname{diam}(K_n)\) shrinks or that \(K_n\) is first-order equivalent to \(W_n\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Universal exact coverage is valid, but the frozen Hausdorff claim is too strong on lower-dimensional observable charts. Because the deviance is measured from the saturated empirical likelihood, a codimension-r chart contributes a model-fit quadratic and an r+2 degree limit, whereas the frozen Wald ellipse uses only the two target coordinates. The separated-stratum definition does not exclude this case. The locally saturated qualification is therefore necessary and is proved without altering the exact-coverage claim.

prose_updates.tldr: For every fixed finite four-response-type selected proxy model, the response-cycle compiler gives a boundary-complete necessary-and-sufficient test for rigidity of the causal pair \(\tau=(\mathrm{PN},\mathrm{PS})\). Its exhaustive local modes retain inactive endpoints and equal-endpoint split vectors, while the IV design adds zero or active residual states, forest scales, the active-cycle product, and relevance. A one-copy connected-component evaluator then returns a common exact target, an incompatibility report, or two legal same-observable full SCMs; strict-positive twins are required only on interior support charts. The atlas agrees with the published regular proxy formulas and terminates with fixed-alphabet exact bounds relative to effective coefficient-field oracles. Wald inference is valid on separated smooth rigid strata, exact confidence-fiber coverage remains valid at every rank and support transition, and first-order profile--Wald agreement is limited to locally saturated observable charts. The GEUVADIS application is specified as a known-selection IV audit, but numerical classification still requires its released cell table and binarization inputs.

project_justification.gap: Published selected-proxy and IV-plus-proxy formulas identify response-type targets under regular invertibility and separation, but do not decide causal-target constancy across simultaneous rank loss, inactive latent rows, coincident endpoints, forced coefficient zeros, or unknown population margins coupled by response-level shared-instrument equations.
project_justification.niche: The four binary response types form a labeled causal cycle. Factorization uniqueness is stronger than necessary: \(\tau_C\) can be constant while nuisance endpoints or equal-endpoint split vectors move. The relevant object is therefore the target image of the full nonnegative SCM fiber, stratified by observable rank, support, incidence, residual, and cycle data.
project_justification.fill: The exhaustive edge-state atlas proves equality between its finite structural union and each normalized cycle fiber. After connected components are computed, one-copy target projection decides within- and cross-component agreement over the ordered input field, and the cycle-to-SCM lift converts every disagreement into legal observationally equivalent causal models. Exact output bounds, separated-chart Wald inference, and transition-robust exact coverage complete the operational map; profile--Wald Hausdorff equivalence is asserted only where the observable chart is locally saturated.

sampling_model.overlap: All population selected-table cells are positive, so every \(v_e(z)\) used for normalization is positive and every compatible population cell margin is positive. Wald inference additionally requires an incident rigid chart with slack at least \(\varepsilon\), twice continuously differentiable continuation, separation from incompatible chart closures, and \(\lambda_{\min}(V_{\tau})\ge\varepsilon\). Boundary and transition laws remain covered by confidence-fiber inversion without rank stability. First-order equivalence of that inversion to the frozen Wald ellipse additionally requires a locally saturated observable chart.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Reduced multinomial coordinates use empirical frequencies and the block-diagonal plug-in covariance. The deterministic chart rule reports a Wald ellipse only after a separated rigid chart and positive-definite sandwich are certified; otherwise it reports the full-square fallback. Transition inference uses exact multinomial replicate tails, a Bonferroni Clopper--Pearson preliminary region, and Berger--Boos calibration over the complete causal target fiber.

prose_updates.related_work: Shingaki, Yoshida, and Kuroki (2026), Theorem 1 and Appendix equations (A.28)--(A.33), supply the selected four-response-type model and regular PN/PS inversions; the atlas proof establishes agreement on compatible laws there and extends the decision domain to all nonnegative rank/support faces. Shingaki and Kuroki (2023) identify all four response-type probabilities in a randomized no-selection proxy experiment, and the established experimental reduction verifies the exact label-converted overlap plus a selected assignment-boundary law. Kawakami (2021), Figure 2(b), equation (2), and Theorem 1(i)--(iii), identify binary potential-outcome types under regular IV-plus-proxy matrix conditions; the overlap theorem derives the same PN/PS transformation and separately exhibits a selected rigid law with singular \(A_x^{\mathrm K}\), a scope separation rather than a subsumption claim. NMF rigidity and partial-identifiability results concern factor recovery, whereas this theorem classifies a causal target on a labeled shared-endpoint cycle. Basu, Pollack, and Roy (2006) supply the classical exact sign, sampling, projection, and connected-component algorithms used only after the causal structural charts have been proved exhaustive.
prose_updates.interpretation: Rigidity means that every full SCM compatible with the causal graph, selected law, and supplied information has the same PN/PS pair; it is not defined by an inverse formula or by uniqueness of the latent proxy factorization. A rigid certificate is therefore an identifying map from observables to the singleton causal target image. A nonrigid certificate consists of two legal full SCMs that agree on all supplied observables and margins but disagree on the causal target. An empty fiber is model incompatibility and is reported separately rather than being labeled rigid or nonidentified.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact structural theorem is finite-alphabet and its real-algebraic component evaluator has a conservative doubly-exponential worst-case envelope; no claim of numerical efficiency is made. Arbitrary real inputs are handled relative to effective arithmetic and sign oracles for their ordered coefficient field, while integer-polynomial bit bounds require explicitly rational encodings. The compiler returns a field expression only when its arithmetic actually constructs one and otherwise retains a real-univariate/Thom encoding. Wald conclusions exclude repeated-root, incompatible-chart, and singular-covariance regimes. Exact confidence coverage remains valid there, but confidence fibers need not shrink at genuinely nonidentified laws.
